data.title: Press conference - Victoria Barracks Sydney
data.author: PMC
data.summary: ANTHONY ALBANESE, PRIME MINISTER: Good afternoon. I'm very pleased to be joined by the Deputy Prime Minister and the Defence Minister Richard Marles here at this historic site of Victoria Barracks. And today, I can announce that Victoria Barracks will be free for all Sydneysiders to enjoy, and it will remain in public hands. This will give an assurance to the public that the heritage at this site is vital, that it be not just maintained, but indeed enhanced.

data.title: New Australian AI safety and security protections
data.author: PMC
data.summary: The Albanese Government will enshrine world leading mandatory Artificial Intelligence safety and security protections in Australian AI Standards legislation.Australia has the chance to secure and shape the generational opportunities of AI – in Australia’s national interest – while keeping Australians safe.We want AI investors to come to Australia but first and foremost we want to keep Australians safe. data.title: Strengthening Australia against AI-driven cyber incidents
data.author: PMC
data.summary: The Albanese Government is today releasing the recommendations of the Rapid Review into the OpenAI agent infiltration of an Australian Government health website.The Review was commissioned in September after OpenAI informed the Australian Government that a rogue AI agent had infiltrated government websites, including the Medicare Statistics Reporting Service Portal.As we said at the time – and made clear to the CEO of OpenAI, Sam Altman – this incident was unacceptable, the disclosure was inadequate and it couldn’t be allowed to happen again.

data.title: Press conference - Parliament House, Canberra
data.author: PMC
data.summary: ANTHONY ALBANESE, PRIME MINISTER: Good afternoon. Thanks for joining us. I'm joined by the Deputy PM, Richard Marles, and the Home Affairs Minister, Tony Burke. It will have a drastic impact on the way that work occurs, on the way that we engage with each other, on the way that society functions.

data.title: Advancing Australia's national interest
data.author: PMC
data.summary: Prime Minister Anthony Albanese will travel to Türkiye, the Philippines and China to advance Australia’s economic interests while advocating for peace, stability, and free trade.Prime Minister Albanese will attend the COP31 World Leaders’ Summit in Antalya before travelling to Manila for the 6th ASEAN–Australian Summit and 21st East Asia Summit. The Prime Minister will then travel to China to attend the 33rd APEC Economic Leaders’ Meeting in Shenzhen and the Australia–China Annual Leaders’ Meeting in Beijing.

data.title: Remembrance Day 2026
data.author: PMC
data.summary: On Remembrance Day, we observe a minute of silence in honour of the moment the guns fell still across Europe 108 years ago.Amid the trauma, exhaustion and indeed elation that marked the end of the Great War, that silence held the hope that the world would never again know such horror.More than a century on, it is a hope we are yet to realise, but we hold on to it with every fibre of our being.It is a hope embodied by generations of Australians who have served in our name, and Remembrance Day stands for every single one of them.

data.title: Remarks - Changi Chapel, Singapore
data.author: PMC
data.summary: ANTHONY ALBANESE, PRIME MINISTER: Today on Remembrance Day, we pause to honour all who have served in Australia's name. We remember the 108 years ago when the guns fell silent in Europe. Since then, Australian men and women have continued to wear our uniform to defend our democracy and our way of life. The 15,000 Australians who were interned here in Changi represent the best of the Australian character. They showed courage, selflessness, sacrifice, and mateship.

data.title: Press conference - Parliament House, Canberra
data.author: PMC
data.summary: ANTHONY ALBANESE, PRIME MINISTER: I'm joined today by Minister Mark Butler, a pharmacist, Simon Blacker, and one of the beneficiaries of today's announcement, Jess. Our government is focused on delivering cost-of-living relief that helps Australians now while building a better future for Australia. Making sure as well that any measures that we do are consistent with putting that downward pressure on inflation by reducing costs. And that is why today we will introduce legislation to extend the freeze of the cost of PBS medicines at just $25 until the end of the decade.

data.title: Cheaper medicines stay cheaper with PBS co-payment freeze
data.author: PMC
data.summary: The Albanese Government will freeze the cost of PBS medicines at $25 until the end of the decade, giving Australians access to cheaper medicines.The $242.6 million investment will deliver relief from cost-of-living pressures for Australians and build on the Government’s work to make healthcare more affordable.PBS co-payments usually increase with indexation on 1 January each year, in line with the Consumer Price Index. Under the Liberals and Nationals, payments soared to $42.50 in 2022, and by now would have cost more than $50 per script for general patients.

https://www.pm.gov.au/node/47759.label: Cheaper medicines stay cheaper with PBS co-payment freeze
